title: Joe Petit, Yank Johnson and loud trombone playing; the Darcys
summary: Joe Petit's old age recording, loud players like Yank Johnson, and the Darcy brothers in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Oh, Lord. One time I made a record of him, honey, was so old that he could hardly play. He played the sound without any teeth, no false teeth. He played both? He played just on the ground, not so well. No. The trouble was this. He was quite deaf. He could hardly hear. And one number they started out, he couldn't even hear what key they were playing in. Oh, I see. He started in the wrong key. Then when he found out what key it was, he heard it finally and changed. Yeah. But he made a couple of numbers just to see how he would sound. Nothing I was ever going to issue, but that was 1944, 1945. Oh, yeah. Joe Petit. And he played Careless Love and St. Louis Blues. When he was young, I guess he used the valve trombone. Yeah, that's right.
That's what he used to hear.
But he used slide when he...

Joe Petit was a fellow for him. He had a good tone, too, on trombone. And they had another fellow that I played with, Joe Petit, named Yank Johnson. That's Buddy Johnson's brother. That Yank had... They could put some of the powerfulest tones in the trombone. They didn't think about sweetness, you know, or nothing like that. They just blasted out. I mean, they could blast them, too. Too loud, you know. On a parade, it was all right. Yeah, in a parade, it was all right. But, you know, playing in a dance or in a place where a party was, you couldn't do that. You could do it, too, but the people didn't like it so well. You played nice and soft. The music is sweet, you know. We had a lot of boys, you see. I'm going to start telling them fellas how to play trombone. Because I listened to them covered in white. Some of them wouldn't do it on trombone. Some of them handle the instrument, all right. But, you know, they don't understand how to take advantage of it, see. They don't take advantage of it. They just blow, blow, blow. Now, I tell you, a fella plays a nice trombone. This fella, them two brothers, what is his name? They play downtown all the time. Here in town now? Tom and Darcy? That's it.
No, he plays a nice trombone. He plays pretty good. Yeah, he gets a pretty tone.
Yeah, he gets a nice tone. And his brother, the trumpet player, out there.

Yeah, clarinet jimmy d'arcy. He plays a nice trombone. He's good. Don't have no whole lot of loud noise, you know, and all like that. I heard him play solo. I heard him play the number behind the band. And with the band, I heard him play the number. And he's good. Do most of the bands play too loud, do you think? Yeah, they could gauge themselves. They could gauge. You know, some fella won't argue. I won't argue you. I want to be seen. I want the people to see me playing better than you allowed. And you see. And I get up there and I ain't going to let you play your part right because I'm going to try to go over you and all that stuff. When they play together, then you'll find out. Nice.
